answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A pearl delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A dawn check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A forge penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 5840 identities need 5840 bonds of 23 tokens, 51157 dollars of hardware and 28 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
